goal: nano-mcp: an MCP server + small SDK so any AI agent can hold XNO and pay per API call in Nano, through rpc.nano.to

laws.statement: Seed-based address derivation matches the official Nano example.
laws.test: tests verify seed->address derivation against official docs.nano.org examples: seed->priv (the-basics blake2b vector), priv->pub and pub->address (key-management key_expand example), plus address encoding against rpc.nano.to account_key ground truth and a live account_key round-trip of a derived SDK account.

laws.statement: Live balance/history reads work through rpc.nano.to without a local node.
laws.test: a test posts account_balance to NANO_RPC_URL for a known public account and asserts a numeric raw balance returns.

laws.statement: A signed send block is accepted and confirms on-chain via rpc.nano.to.
laws.test: nano_sdk test sends a tiny self-transfer and asserts rpc process returns a block hash later present in account_history.

laws.statement: The SDK refuses to send more than the wallet holds and never exceeds the 0.01 XNO/day outbound cap.
laws.test: unit test calls send with amount > balance and with an amount that would breach the daily cap; both raise.

laws.statement: The server derives a distinct, reproducible one-time payment address per request_id.
laws.test: test calls the derivation with two request_ids and asserts addresses differ, and repeats one id asserting the same address.

laws.statement: verify_payment(request_id) approves only after the on-chain send to that address is seen, exactly once.
laws.test: test drives a send to a derived address then verify_payment returns approved; a second verify_payment for the same id returns spent/not-approved.

laws.statement: An end-to-end pay-per-call succeeds and is replay-safe (single execution).
laws.test: probe scenario has one agent pay one service via the SDK and MCP server, then re-calls with the same request_id and observes no double execution.

laws.statement: External payments are journaled as nano_tx while own accounts are never logged.
laws.test: a test hits the journal gate: one nano_tx row lands in a scratch journal db for an external payer and zero rows for an account in NANO_AGENT_OWN_ACCOUNTS.

laws.statement: A USD-priced quote returns an exact XNO amount computed from the MEDIAN of three independent public price sources, and never holds or converts anyone's money.
laws.test: test calls a pricing function with three injected XNO/USD rates and asserts the returned raw XNO amount equals ceil(usd/median * 10^30); a live network test fetches CoinGecko, CoinPaprika and Kucoin and asserts a numeric USD median returns; the quote path performs no balance change or transfer (pure computation).

laws.statement: A dollar quote expires in 30 seconds or less.
laws.test: test mints a quote with an injectable clock at t, asserting expires_at - t <= 30s; a second test advances the clock past expires_at and asserts verify_payment returns status='expired' and does not approve.

laws.statement: A buyer session spends only under a valid owner-signed, unexpired mandate bound to its own sub-account.
laws.test: tests/test_buyer.py: a valid mandate authorizes a send; tampered signature, wrong owner key, expired, or mis-bound mandate raise before the client records any process call.

laws.statement: The buyer SDK enforces a per-session cap, the daily cap, and the balance guard before broadcast.
laws.test: tests/test_buyer.py: a send over the session cap, over the daily 0.01 XNO cap, or over the on-chain balance raises with no client process call recorded; sending up to the session cap is allowed and recorded.

laws.statement: Every published scorecard figure is reproduced exactly by rerunning the scorecard build on the published raw data.
laws.test: tests/test_scorecard.py: test_l13_verify_passes_on_published_raw_data builds then verify() returns ok with no problems; test_l13_verify_detects_figure_drift corrupts a published rail figure and verify() fails; test_cli_build_and_verify_is_reproducible runs 'python -m nano_mcp.scorecard build' then 'verify' via subprocess and asserts exit 0 with 'verify PASS'.

laws.statement: The scorecard's Nano share counts only external nano receipts plus public x402 counts, own traffic excluded.
laws.test: tests/test_scorecard.py test_l12_share_counts_only_external_receipts: external_receipts==1 and share==1/(165000000+1) with an own-account row contributing zero; test_l12_own_traffic_adds_exactly_zero_to_share: share==0 for both all-own and empty journal; count_external_receipts returns only external payers.

laws.statement: P1's x402 exact-on-nano spec is prepared and verified, ready to open only after human approval.
laws.test: tests/test_x402_draft.py passes (8): the spec at draft/x402/specs/schemes/exact/scheme_exact_nano.md has every required x402 section, its JSON examples parse and agree on network=nano:live/asset=XNO/scheme=exact, it encodes at-least-two-RPC confirmation that fails closed and an exactly-once claim, and pending.md frames the contribution as the exact scheme on the nano network and opens no PR; full suite 86 passed.

laws.statement: P1's x402 exact-on-nano reference implementation draft is prepared and verified, ready to open only after human approval.
laws.test: tests/test_x402_draft_refimpl.py passes: the draft TS package at draft/x402/typescript/packages/mechanisms/nano implements the SchemeNetworkClient/Server/Facilitator interfaces (type-checks with 'tsc --noEmit' against the published @x402/core, exercised via subprocess), encodes network=nano:live / asset=XNO / paymentProof 64-hex, fail-closed >=2-independent-RPC verification, an atomic single-use claim, and pending.md frames the reference-implementation contribution and opens no PR; full suite passes.

laws.statement: The facilitator exposes /supported /verify /settle per the exact-on-nano spec and fails closed unless a proof confirms on at least two independent RPC endpoints.
laws.test: tests/test_facilitator.py: test_l16_facilitator_exposes_supported_verify_settle; test_l16_verify_confirms_on_two_independent_endpoints; test_l16_fail_closed_when_any_endpoint_errors; test_l16_refuses_less_than_two_endpoints; test_l16_http_get_supported; test_l16_http_post_verify_confirms_on_two_endpoints

laws.statement: Settle re-verifies on-chain then binds a proof to its request with an atomic single-use claim, so one proof settles exactly once.
laws.test: tests/test_facilitator.py: test_l17_settle_re_verifies_then_claims_atomically; test_l17_settle_never_trusts_prior_verify; test_l17_claim_store_persists_exactly_once_across_instances; test_l17_concurrent_settles_approve_exactly_once; test_l17_http_post_settle_exactly_once

laws.statement: The multi-RPC verifier parses the real Nano block_info shape and confirms a real on-chain send on two independent public endpoints.
laws.test: verify_block_on_independent_endpoints confirms a real confirmed Nano send block on two independent public RPCs with a non-empty payer; an incomplete/malformed node response is refused, not passed.

laws.statement: The nano exact resource server returns HTTP 402 with a payment-required header then serves the protected result once its payment proof is settled
laws.test: tests/test_httpx402.py drives a real in-process HTTP server: the first GET returns 402 with a payment-required header carrying the nano exact requirement (scheme exact, network nano:live, asset XNO, a one-time nano_ payTo and the exact raw amount), and after the client retries with a payment-signature payload that the facilitator verifies then settles the server returns 200 with the protected result and a payment-response header; a wire client pay_and_fetch completes the two-request dance. Full suite 130 passes.

laws.statement: A spent payment proof is refused so one payment never serves the resource twice
laws.test: tests/test_httpx402.py replays the same spent payment-signature header a second time and asserts HTTP 402 with the protected result absent, because the facilitator's atomic single-use claim consumes the one proof exactly once.

laws.statement: The MCP paidTool wrapper refuses a spent or replayed payment proof, so one payment never serves a protected tool result twice.
laws.test: tests/test_paidtool.py: calling paid_tool_execute twice with the same request_id/paymentProof returns ok on the first and refused on the second, and the second returns no protected result — the facilitator's atomic single-use claim consumes the proof exactly once across MCP calls.

laws.statement: The paidTool wrapper issues a one-time nano payTo then serves the result only after the proof is verified and settled on two RPCs.
laws.test: tests/test_paidtool.py drives the real MCPServer in-process (mcp v2): paid_tool_request returns a distinct one-time nano_ payTo + exact amount per call; paid_tool_execute with a 64-hex proof the stub nodes confirm on both endpoints returns the protected result exactly once; fail-closed when one of two endpoints errors; wrong amount or missing requestId refused. Full suite 130+ passes.
